summary: Yakima County summit on the Cascade crest: 1934 L-4 cab, removed or destroyed in 1952; Willhite's photo captions show footings and the summit is now reached by trail.

facts.design: Frame tower with observation cab; 16-by-16-foot L-4 cab built 1934 (Willhite)
facts.status_note: Cab removed or destroyed in 1952 (sources differ on which); photo captions on Willhite's page show footings on the summit rock

visit.trail_note: Reached on foot from the Midway PCT trailhead; Willhite lists 1.8 miles and about 800 feet of gain, and says the old road is now a trail, overgrown in places. No source says whether the summit is open to visitors.

events.note: 16-by-16-foot L-4 cab built (Willhite); firetower.org and FireLookout.com date the tower to the 1930s
Garage built and panoramic photos taken from the roof in the same year (Willhite)
Firetower.org says the tower was removed in 1952; Forest Lookouts lists it as removed, without a year
FireLookout.com and Willhite say destroyed in 1952
Registered August 11, 2012 as US 1373, WA 273; nominated by Ray Kresek

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firetower.org and Forest Lookouts say removed; FireLookout.com and Willhite say destroyed. Not resolved; the story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Four sources, but Willhite carries nearly all the detail. No staffing or fire history appears in the sources read, so none is written. The 1952 removed-or-destroyed split is unresolved. The footings and the 2018 garage come from photo captions with no capture dates. Willhite's panorama captions say July 7, 1934, and a National Archives caption on Firetower.org says 7-27-1934; not used in the story. Access level is omitted because no source says whether the summit is public or closed.
